historyReviewBoundary: All 115 histories have author source checks. Final independent review covered metadata and numerical checks for all 115 classes, 12 deeper class targets and source-gap samples in seven classes. It did not independently verify every passage of every cited source.

history.name: Statins (HMG-CoA reductase inhibitors)

starting.description: Cholesterol/disease biology motivated a deliberate microbial-inhibitor search. Observed inhibition of cholesterol synthesis by fungal ML-236 metabolites supplied the working lead from which the statin class developed.

inspiration.description: Fungal metabolites with observed cholesterol-synthesis inhibition, within a pathway/disease-motivated investigation.

steps.description: The investigators sought microbial substances that specifically inhibited cholesterol synthesis.
The search yielded ML-236 metabolites from Penicillium citrinum, opening the fungal statin lineage.
The class later included semisynthetic and synthetic members, preserving its founding natural-product ancestry at class level.
Endo identifies lovastatin's 1987 approval as the first commercial statin, followed by the later members summarized in the conclusion.

design.description: Development established natural, semisynthetic and wholly synthetic later statins. Those chemical routes are later contributions within the observation-led class; this bounded record does not reconstruct each analogue's modifications.

circumstances.description: The documented microbial search deliberately sought inhibitors of cholesterol synthesis. The selected passages do not establish an accidental class-founding finding.

sources.citation: Endo A, Kuroda M, Tsujita Y. 1976. ML-236A, ML-236B, and ML-236C, new inhibitors of cholesterogenesis produced by Penicillium citrinum. DOI 10.7164/antibiotics.29.1346; PMID 1010803.
Endo A. 2010. A historical perspective on the discovery of statins. DOI 10.2183/pjab.86.484.
Alberts AW et al. 1980. Mevinolin: a highly potent competitive inhibitor of hydroxymethylglutaryl-coenzyme A reductase and a cholesterol-lowering agent. DOI 10.1073/pnas.77.7.3957; PMID 6933445.

evidence.locator: p.1346, opening paragraph; line wrap normalized
p.490, clinical development, immediately before conclusion

limits: The founding fungal activity/lead is the class-history unit. This is not a claim that every later statin was isolated from a fungus or shares an unchanged natural structure.
The disease/pathway rationale is contextual; no historical epidemiological effect estimate is independently evaluated here.
Multiple synthetic/semisynthetic manufacturing and medicinal-chemistry routes do not by themselves make the discovery basis mixed.
gaps: The mevinolin1980 original was read at abstract extent only. This bounded reconciliation does not adjudicate every early priority claim or individual analogue chemistry.

humanContributionInterpretation.summary: Human cholesterol-disease evidence supplied a therapeutic rationale for cholesterol lowering; Endo explicitly names Framingham and describes the resulting search for inhibitors.
humanContributionInterpretation.scope: Population evidence supplied the rationale; fungal screening supplied the molecular lead. Framingham was a contributor, not the sole discovery event.
